public_rationale: Pre-publication interviews document abrupt Replika changes and users experiencing substantial grief and revived rejection trauma. That supports the claim under the stated reading of 'arbitrary'. [ABC reporting](https://www.abc.net.au/news/science/2023-03-01/replika-users-fell-in-love-with-their-ai-chatbot-companion/102028196). Regulatory intervention means the changes should not be described as demonstrably reasonless. [Official notice](https://www.garanteprivacy.it/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/9852506).
limitations: Support depends on interpreting 'arbitrary' as imposed unexpectedly, rather than without any justification.
The accounts establish some users' reported distress, not its prevalence or a diagnosed condition.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Companion chatbots have already been changed arbitrarily in ways that left some users in serious emotional pain.

statement.excerpt: Chatbot companions that offer emotional support have already been changed in arbitrary ways that left some users in serious emotional pain.

from_speaker: Chatbot companions that offer emotional support
left some users in serious emotional pain
our_interpretation: 'Already' describes events before publication, with no stated starting date.
'Arbitrary' is read as unexpected changes imposed without meaningful user control. It does not require proving the company had no rationale.
Serious emotional pain means credible reports of substantial grief or distress; a clinical diagnosis is not required.
The claim concerns some users, not all users or a population-level incidence rate.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish pre-publication changes to emotional-support companions and credible user accounts link those changes to substantial grief or distress.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records refute the relevant changes or establish that the reported distress did not occur or was unrelated to them.
